overview: The Medford Public Schools School Committee is the governing body responsible for setting district policy, approving the operating and capital budgets, overseeing collective bargaining, and directing district-wide facility planning. Over the 97 meetings held between July 2023 and October 2026, the committee conducted its work across three terms, addressing district administration, aging school infrastructure, curriculum and student policies, and chronic capacity constraints. The body navigated executive transitions, appointing an interim superintendent who was subsequently appointed permanent superintendent, and repeatedly remediated budget shortfalls alongside local ballot initiatives. Concurrently, the committee oversaw multi-million dollar HVAC overhauls across elementary and middle schools and advanced the comprehensive Medford High School building project through MSBA eligibility and schematic design phases. At its most recent meeting, the committee voted to advance geothermal HVAC systems and specialized construction delivery methods for elementary repairs, reviewed expanded after-school program operations, and monitored first-quarter district spending.

threads.name: Medford High School building project
threads.summary: In late 2023, Superintendent Edouard-Vincent announced that Medford High School was accepted into the MSBA core program eligibility phase [M11#5]. The committee established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee in early 2024, setting project goals, voting positions, and leadership [M15#5, M16#4, M16#5]. Through 2025, the committee authorized an MSBA feasibility study agreement for a 1,395-student capacity [M52#7], selected Left Field as Owner's Project Manager [M60#5], and approved Left Field invoices while beginning designer evaluations [M65#2, M65#3]. In 2026, the body approved the high school educational plan [M77#3], modified design alternatives to respect a 1967 DCR deed restriction barring construction on Edgley Field [M85#2, M88#3], approved educational plan adjustments and LEED v4 Silver sustainability goals [M90#7, M92#7], and reconstituted building committee membership for the schematic design phase [M93#9].

threads.name: Superintendent leadership and contract
threads.summary: The committee held multiple executive sessions across mid-2024 regarding strategy for contract negotiations with Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent [M31#2, M33#2, M38#1]. In December 2024, the committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as interim superintendent following Superintendent Edouard-Vincent's departure [M47#2, M48#3, M49#9], approving her interim contract in January 2025 [M49#3]. The committee evaluated Interim Superintendent Galusi's performance and transitional goals through early 2026 [M68#13, M74#8, M76#6]. In February 2026, the committee voted to appoint Dr. Galusi as permanent superintendent pending contract negotiations [M77#4], subsequently approving a three-year contract in May 2026 and realigning the superintendent evaluation cadence with the academic year [M83#6, M90#11].

threads.name: District budget development and stabilization
threads.summary: In early 2024, the committee addressed a projected $2.5 million FY24 budget deficit, resolving it to $216,000 through encumbrance corrections and postponed spending [M15#4, M18#5]. The committee approved a level-service FY25 budget request of $79,399,774 before finalizing a $77.75 million operating budget and adopting a formal eight-phase budget schedule policy [M25#9, M27#9, M29#7]. Following voter approval of ballot questions 7 and 8, the committee adopted a supplemental budget appropriation in January 2025 to restore positions and fund reserves [M36#8, M44#7, M49#7]. Facing projected municipal and school gaps for FY27, the committee deliberated school stabilization funds with the City Council and adopted an adjusted FY27 budget closing an $833,398 deficit [M81#2, M81#3, M90#4], later reviewing first-quarter encumbrances and special education transit risks [M97#6].

threads.name: HVAC and building infrastructure overhauls
threads.summary: After reviewing severe cooling failures across aging buildings in late 2023 [M03#6], the committee approved a $15 to $20 million partial-decarbonization scope for the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools [M23#6]. The committee passed a policy ending unauthorized purchases of fossil-fuel building equipment [M23#13], authorized construction management at risk [M44#6], and approved bond requests totaling over $25.7 million for the McGlynn and Andrews projects [M48#6, M57#7]. Following a facilities condition assessment identifying $83.7 million in district repair needs [M71#3], the committee submitted MSBA Accelerated Repair statements of interest for three elementary schools [M55#1], approved a $22.7 million schematic design and CMR delivery for Roberts Elementary [M93#4, M97#5], and selected ground-source geothermal heat pumps for Missituk Elementary [M97#4].

threads.name: Elementary overcrowding and grade configuration
threads.summary: In September 2024, staff and committee members addressed severe overcrowding at Roberts Elementary School, where enrollment exceeded 590 students, prompting calls for redistricting [M34#8, M35#6]. In spring 2025, the committee referred elementary capacity reviews to subcommittee [M58#4], approved relocating preschool classrooms out of Roberts to Missituk Elementary, and established a space planning task force [M63#6, M63#7]. The body evaluated a space utilization study proposing K-4, 5-6, and 7-8 restructuring and collected community survey feedback [M72#5, M73#5]. In July 2026, the committee voted to postpone any 5-8 middle school reconfiguration to the 2028-2029 school year [M92#4], and in autumn 2026 debated a draft policy to formalize alternative elementary school placements [M96#5].

threads.name: Student transportation operations and safety
threads.summary: In late 2023, the committee initiated a community transportation survey to evaluate busing needs [M07#8, M20#1]. Severe regional driver shortages from vendor Eastern Bus repeatedly caused route overcrowding and eligibility disruptions in autumn 2024 [M34#12, M35#8, M40#4]. In June 2025, the committee approved a new five-year yellow bus contract with Eastern Bus while referring electrification planning to subcommittee [M64#4]. To address ongoing safety and transit behavior, the committee requested municipal adoption of bus stop-arm enforcement cameras [M67#8] and implemented an internal monitoring plan utilizing rotating paraprofessionals [M69#5, M70#6], later reviewing student advisory proposals for bus stop railings and late bus service [M72#3, M96#4].

threads.name: Graduation requirements and assessment policy
threads.summary: Following district reviews of MCAS accountability data [M07#7, M43#5], the committee passed a resolution in September 2024 endorsing state Question 2 to remove MCAS as a high school graduation requirement [M36#8]. In February 2025, following the ballot question's passage, the committee approved the first reading of Policy IKF replacing the MCAS competency requirement with aligned coursework [M52#3], granting second reading approval later that month [M54#7]. The committee adopted further amendments to Policy IKF to clarify math sequence requirements and ceremony participation for students receiving certificates of completion [M57#6, M58#3], and officially rescinded the legacy policy IKFC-MCAS [M64#9].

threads.name: Career and Technical Education admissions and expansion
threads.summary: In May 2024, the committee voted to direct the School Building Committee to explore CTE expansions as part of the MSBA feasibility study [M25#8], later adjusting timelines and dropping veterinary science from the Chapter 74 expansion plan [M54#6]. Facing oversubscribed vocational majors, the committee approved an admissions policy establishing a straight, non-weighted lottery system for vocational enrollment [M69#3, M70#4]. In 2026, the committee updated the Chapter 74 admissions policy based on state guidance regarding lottery procedures and retention pathways [M82#3], approved an updated Chapter 74 viability form for the MSBA [M91#1], and reviewed an honors pilot enabling juniors and seniors to earn honors credit through co-ops or capstone projects [M94#4].

threads.name: Before and after-school childcare expansion
threads.summary: In early 2024, the committee approved minor rate adjustments for childcare programs and requested waitlist and capacity updates [M17#7, M39#8, M44#3]. In May 2025, the body authorized an expansion plan partnering with the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) to eliminate waitlists [M61#2], while introducing an early-pickup rate and expanding site coordinators to full-time status [M64#5, M66#3]. Based on the completed BASIC recommendations, the committee approved adding 150 seats, introducing specialized curriculum staff, and adjusting the program rate card [M83#4, M83#5]. By autumn 2026, the administration reported a 50 percent increase in overall enrollment and a 68 percent reduction in the after-school waitlist [M94#5, M97#3].
